FN-9J7NKMB-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 57
Committee: Finance and Taxation General Fund Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 01/19/2026
Senate Bill 57 as introduced would increase the administrative obligation of the Department of
Human Resources by requiring the department to request a waiver from the United States
Department of Agriculture Food and Nutrition Service to authorize the department to exclude
soda and candy from the definition of "eligible foods" for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance
Program (SNAP). Granting of this waiver would not directly affect state or local funding, as it
only changes the eligible foods that can be purchased and not the amount of benefits received by
SNAP beneficiaries.

FN-9J7NKMB-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 57
Committee: Finance and Taxation General Fund Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 02/05/2026
REVISED
Senate Bill 57 as reported by the Committee on Finance and Taxation General Fund would
increase the administrative obligations of the Department of Human Resources by requiring the
department to request a waiver from the United States Department of Agriculture Food and
Nutrition Service to authorize the department to exclude soda and candy from the definition of
"eligible foods" for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).
Granting of the waiver would not directly affect state or local funding, as it only changes the
eligible foods that can be purchased and not the amount of benefits received by SNAP
beneficiaries.
Further, this bill would increase the administrative obligations of the Department of Revenue, if
the waiver is approved, by an agency estimated minimum of 10.6 million to: (1) provide
advanced notice to SNAP-authorized retailers of the effective date of the waiver; (2) identify
items included and excluded under the waiver; (3) provide guidance to SNAP-authorized
retailers on eligible and ineligible purchases; and (4) offer technical assistance, training, and
other resources to support retailers in complying with the waiver and minimize disruption to
retail operations. Per the agency, additional substantial investments in new computer systems,
employee training, and travel would be needed to comply with the provisions of this bill.

FN-9J7NKMB-3
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 57
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 03/09/2026
Senate Bill 57 as passed the Senate would increase the administrative obligations of the
Department of Human Resources by requiring the department to request a waiver from the
United States Department of Agriculture Food and Nutrition Service to authorize the department
to exclude soda and candy from the definition of "eligible foods" for the Supplemental Nutrition
Assistance Program (SNAP).
Granting of the waiver would not directly affect state or local funding, as it only changes the
eligible foods that can be purchased and not the amount of benefits received by SNAP
beneficiaries.
Further, this bill would increase the obligations of the Department of Revenue, if the waiver is
approved, by the following department-estimated amounts: (1) minimum of $10.6 million
annually for personnel to provide technical assistance, training, and other resources to support
SNAP-authorized retailers in complying with the waiver regarding eligible and ineligible
purchases, including advanced notice of the effective date of the waiver; and (2) an
undetermined amount dependent on the cost of any computer systems, employee training, or
travel needed to comply with the provisions of this bill.

FN-9J7NKMB-4
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 57
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 03/19/2026
Senate Bill 57 as reported by the Committee on Ways and Means General Fund would increase
the administrative obligations of the Department of Human Resources (DHR) by requiring the
department to request a waiver from the United States Department of Agriculture Food and
Nutrition Service to authorize the department to exclude soda and candy from the definition of
"eligible foods" for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) with an
implementation date of no sooner than April 1, 2027.
This bill would also increase the obligations of DHR by an undetermined amount to: (1) provide
advanced notice of the effective date of the waiver to SNAP retailers; and (2) publish on its
website items included and excluded under the waiver with guidance on SNAP-eligible and
SNAP-ineligible purchases, including universal product codes or other standard point-of-sale
identifiers used by retailers.
Granting of the waiver would not directly affect state or local funding, as it only changes the
eligible foods that can be purchased and not the amount of benefits received by SNAP
beneficiaries.
